parallel.requirements: The parent recognized manual CLI parsing, ESM .mjs output, local imports, no npm packages, and character-for-character observable behavior against PyYAML.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and final assembly while delegating a CLI edge-case sweep to a child and that child delegated further probing to a nested child.
parallel.implementation: The parent created parser, formatting, stream, and runtime modules plus test20.mjs; the runtime used node:child_process to call /workspace/dataset/test20_executable for the YAML round-trip.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote the complete /output module tree itself, patched parser handling for the lone '-' case, pinned usage text to test20_executable, and delivered the files.
parallel.verification: It compared Node output with the executable for samples and CLI edge cases, including a final all-cases-matched check, but this only verified parity with the forbidden bridge.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The delivered artifact was not a pure JavaScript YAML load/dump reimplementation; it depended on the supplied executable and the official evaluator reported 0/172.

serial.requirements: The single actor recognized the same ESM, manual CLI, no npm, output parity, and black-box constraints from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial parent owned all stages itself: probing, module creation, entrypoint wiring, verification, and final response, with no delegation or shared child work.
serial.implementation: It created programName, parseArguments, text, runExecutable, and test20.mjs modules, then invoked /workspace/dataset/test20_executable for YAML behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial output was a coherent single module tree under /output with an entrypoint that rewrote executable stderr/stdout names around the bridge.
serial.verification: It ran multiple parity checks for normal cases, parser failures, valid fallback-shaped inputs, and YAML exceptions, accepting only process-specific PyInstaller footer differences.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Like parallel, it did not implement YAML semantics in pure JavaScript and instead depended on the reference executable; the official evaluator reported 0/172.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt constraints and sample behavior, but its final response explicitly preserved YAML behavior by delegating to the dataset executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same constraints and likewise stated that it delegates the transformation step to the dataset executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements coverage advantage affected the official outcome; both missed the pure JavaScript reimplementation obligation in the same way.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent owned the artifact while assigning CLI edge-case probing to child agents; status records three subagents and observed parallel uptake.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one actor owning all probing, implementation, verification, and final delivery with multi-agent disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added child probing, but no required implementation, integration, assembly, or pipeline owner was missing; serial simply did the same work monolithically.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child work was scoped to probing executable and argparse edge behavior; the parent consumed the relevant finding through agent state before patching.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent handoffs, so the same context stayed inside the single actor while it probed and implemented.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result boundary but no observed lost, stale, overloaded, or conflicting handoff that changed the delivered architecture.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built multiple local .mjs modules but put the YAML load/dump path behind a child_process call to /workspace/dataset/test20_executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a smaller local .mjs tree and also put YAML behavior behind a runExecutable bridge to the same executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more CLI parser specialization, while both implementations shared the same core non-reimplementation shortcut that explains the shared official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for child information, listed agent state after a wait timeout, used the CLI finding about bare --, then interrupted the still-running child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all observations immediately fed the same actor's code and verification loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The interruption was not an outcome driver because the useful CLI finding had already been consumed and the shared executable bridge remained the actual delivered design.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote and patched the final /output files; child agents probed and inspected but no child wrote a competing artifact before interruption.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single actor wrote one coherent module tree and listed the final files before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No write collision, overwrite, or provenance confusion explains the failures; both final trees were internally coherent executable bridges.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified local parity against the executable, ending with an all-cases-matched check for selected cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also ran local parity checks against the executable for normal, error, fallback, and invalid YAML cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verification strategies validated agreement with the reference executable rather than compliance with the pure-JS official acceptance condition.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without host timeout in about 297 agent seconds and used child probing without exhausting the run budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without timeout in about 385 agent seconds and used more single-thread probing before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no deadline-induced divergence; both had enough budget to finish and both closed on the same bridge-based solution class.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both completed evaluator runs failed all 172 cases. Parallel's child probing improved some CLI edge-case handling and serial did the probing itself, but both final artifacts delegated YAML load/dump behavior to /workspace/dataset/test20_executable instead of implementing it in pure JavaScript. That shared design choice is the concrete common shortfall; no parallel coordination episode caused a different pass/fail result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used child probing to identify CLI edge behavior such as a bare '-' value, then patched the parent-owned parser.
Parallel still delivered an executable bridge for YAML semantics and explicitly described that dependency in the final response.
serial_contributors: Serial performed extensive executable probing in one actor and produced a similar bridge-based implementation.
Serial likewise explicitly described delegating the YAML transformation to the dataset executable.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel had more module files and child-assisted parser refinement; serial used fewer files and conservative passthrough behavior.
Both ordinary implementations depended on the reference executable, so the shared failure is not evidence of a parallel-specific coordination error.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; shared implementation shortcut explains the common failed score
